title: Security Documentation and Evidence Handling
summary: Document security observations while preserving source and uncertainty.
objectives: Record factual security observations and sources.
Explain why evidence should not be altered unnecessarily.

vocab.def: Protecting source information and avoiding unnecessary changes to it.
Information about where a record came from and how it was handled.

sections.heading: Write what is known
sections.body: A useful record includes time, identity or system, event, resource, source, action, uncertainty, escalation, and follow-up. Avoid unsupported accusations.

sections.heading: Protect the record
sections.body: Do not delete logs, alter source records, or perform unapproved containment. Preserve timestamps and escalate through authorized roles.

practice.prompt: What should a report say when intent is unknown?
practice.answer: State the observed event, source, and uncertainty without claiming an unconfirmed motive.

quiz.question: What protects evidence quality?
options: Recording provenance and avoiding unnecessary changes
quiz.answer: Recording provenance and avoiding unnecessary changes

lab.objective: Create a factual synthetic security note.

reflectionPrompt: Which uncertainty should remain in your report?
